overview.title: Welcome to Go for 3DS 👋

sections.text: All the pages, in reading order

overview.text: Welcome to Go for 3DS 👋 Go for 3DS runs Go programs on the Nintendo 3DS : a 3D island on the top screen, buttons and sliders you touch on the bottom one, and real 3D with the slider. It is the console's side of the family: the program's loop, the buttons and the touch screen, and a Go UI interface on the bottom screen. Go Renderer draws on the console through its own graphics chip. Programs are built with a special version of TinyGo and opened from the Homebrew Launcher. Is it for me? ✅ You have a 3DS (or an emulator) and want to put your own program on it. ✅ You want to see how one program runs on very small hardware . ❌ You want to play commercial games: this is homebrew, for your own programs. Where to start Pick the line that sounds like you. If you… Read Time are new and want a program on the console 🏴‍☠️ The quest : an island in your pocket, in 5 levels 45 min want to know what each package does and what you need What is where 10 min plan a larger program for the console Before writing a larger program 5 min All the pages, in reading order The menu on the left (or the files in docs/ ) follows this order. Start Overview : this page The quest : five levels, from words on the screen to real 3D What is where : the packages, the explorer, what you need, what was checked, and limits to know before a larger program 🚧 Not done yet See what is where . Words you will meet Word What it means Go A programming language. To try these projects you install it once, from go.dev, and type go run … in a terminal. Terminal The window where you type commands: Terminal on macOS and Linux, PowerShell on Windows. Repository A project's folder of files, kept on GitHub. git clone <address> copies it to your computer. Homebrew Programs for a game console that it was not sold with, opened from the Homebrew Launcher. Quest The tutorial of these docs: short levels, each ending with something that works and an achievement. The family Go for 3DS is one of a family of small projects that work together: Project What it does Go Renderer draws 3D scenes and flat interfaces Go UI buttons, panels and whole applications Go UI for Android Android apps that look like Android's own Go Sound sound and music Go Scene Builder 3D scenes from a flat map Go Simulator simulations that change a scene Go Terrain Simulator ground shaped by rivers Go Climate Simulator weather and biomes Go Flora Simulator forests that grow Go Urban Simulator towns that grow Go Motion Simulator a scene that moves Go for 3DS (this one) Go on the Nintendo 3DS ⚠️ All of them are educational experiments , written with an AI assistant and pending review by their author: good for learning and playing, not for production.

the-quest.title: The 3DS quest
the-quest.text: The 3DS quest Put a Go program on a Nintendo 3DS, one level at a time. Each level teaches one piece of Go for 3DS and ends with a .3dsx you can run in an emulator or on the console. The quest map: a road from START through 5 levels — Homebrewer, Islander, Navigator, Touch designer and Stereoscopist — to a final challenge, Console owner We start with words on the bottom screen, then put Go Renderer's sample island on the top one, turn it with the circle pad, add a Go UI panel to touch below, switch on the real 3D, and finally copy it to an SD card. Every level has the same shape: the idea (explained with something from everyday life), the code , a checkpoint to know it works, and an optional bonus . Before you start You need: Why Where TinyGo with the nintendo3ds target Go does not build for the 3DS; this fork of TinyGo does tinygo-3ds 's releases ( v0.42.0-3ds.1 : LLVM inside, nothing else to install), or built from its main (its NINTENDO3DS.md ) devkitPro's 3DS packages The console's libraries: libctru, citro3d, 3dstools dkp-pacman -S 3ds-dev ( devkitpro.org ); tinygo-3ds finds it in $DEVKITPRO , or /opt/devkitpro An emulator (optional) To try a program without the console Azahar Make a module for the quest and ask for Go for 3DS, which brings the versions of Go Renderer and Go UI that draw on the console with it: mkdir homebrew && cd homebrew go mod init example.com/homebrew go get github.com/akrck02/go-3ds@latest Build any level, and open it: go mod tidy tinygo build -target=nintendo3ds -o hello.3dsx ./hello azahar hello.3dsx Every file starts with //go:build nintendo3ds : these programs only build for the console. Level 1 · The Homebrewer Mission Pieces Time A colour above, words below, and the buttons you press ctr.Open , OpenBottomConsole , app.Run , frames 10 min The idea A game console runs a flip book : sixty pages a second, each drawn and then shown. Your program is called once a page ( app.Run 's function), reads the buttons, draws, and hands the page over ( ctr.EndFrame ), which waits for the screen. Homebrew is a program the console was not sold with, opened from the Homebrew Launcher . Build it hello/main.go : //go:build nintendo3ds // Your first homebrew: a colour on the top screen, words on the bottom one, and the buttons you // press. package main import ( "fmt" "github.com/akrck02/go-3ds/app" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/ctr" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/input" ) // sea is the top screen's colour, 0xRRGGBBAA. const sea = 0x2a6f97ff func main() { screen, err := ctr.Open() // the graphics system and the top screen if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } defer screen.Close() ctr.OpenBottomConsole() // the bottom screen becomes a terminal: what the program prints goes there fmt.Println("Hello from Go!") fmt.Println("Press A, B or the cross. START ends.") keys := []input.Key{input.KeyEnter, input.KeyEscape, input.KeyUp, input.KeyDown, input.KeyLeft, input.KeyRight} names := []string{"A", "B", "up", "down", "left", "right"} app.Run(func(frame app.Frame) bool { for index, key := range keys { if frame.Input.Pressed(key) { fmt.Println("pressed", names[index]) } } ctr.BeginFrame() screen.Clear(sea) ctr.EndFrame() // waits for the screen: one frame each sixtieth of a second return true // false would end the program }) } ctr.Open starts the graphics: always first. app.Run reads the controls into Go Renderer's input.State , the same as on a desktop: A is Enter, B is Escape, the cross is the arrows. Checkpoint The top screen is sea blue; the bottom one says Hello from Go! , and a line for every button you press. START ends the program. Level 1: a blue top screen, and Hello from Go! on the bottom one Bonus (optional): count the frames Achievement unlocked: Homebrewer Level 2 · The Islander Mission Pieces Time The sample island in 3D on the top screen ctr.NewSceneRenderer , Draw , a camera 5 min The idea Go Renderer describes a scene the same way everywhere; only the painter changes. On the desktop it is OpenGL or Metal; on the 3DS it is citro3d, the console's own, through ctr . The scene, the camera and the sample island are the same as on a computer. Build it island/main.go : //go:build nintendo3ds // The sample island on the top screen, seen from a camera that stands still. package main import ( "github.com/akrck02/go-3ds/app" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/ctr" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/graphics" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/models" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene/sample" ) func main() { screen, err := ctr.Open() if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } defer screen.Close() renderer, err := ctr.NewSceneRenderer(screen) // draws a go-renderer scene through citro3d if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } world := sample.Island() // the same made-up island the desktop viewer opens with -sample island view := models.Camera{ Position: graphics.Vec4{300, 220, 300, 1}, // metres east, up and south of the middle Target: graphics.Vec4{0, 0, 0, 1}, Up: graphics.Vec4{0, 1, 0, 0}, Far: 20000, } app.Run(func(frame app.Frame) bool { renderer.Draw(world, view) // begins the frame, draws and shows it return true }) } Checkpoint The island in the middle of the sea, with its forest and village, under a hazy sky. Level 2: the island on the top screen Achievement unlocked: Islander Learn more: Go Renderer on the 3DS Level 3 · The Navigator Mission Pieces Time Turn round the island with the circle pad frame.Reading.Circle , camera.Orbit 6 min The idea The circle pad is a joystick: it says how far it is pushed each way, from −1 to 1. The orbit camera is the desktop viewer's: it circles round a point, and here the pad turns it instead of the mouse. The cross and L , R already speak the camera's language: arrows and minus, plus. Build it //go:build nintendo3ds // The island on the top screen, turned with the circle pad and the cross, nearer and further with // L and R. package main import ( "github.com/akrck02/go-3ds/app" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/camera" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/ctr" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/graphics" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/input" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/models" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene/sample" ) func main() { screen, err := ctr.Open() if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } defer screen.Close() renderer, err := ctr.NewSceneRenderer(screen) if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } world := sample.Island() orbit := camera.NewOrbit(graphics.Vec4{0, 0, 0, 1}, 450) // the desktop viewer's orbit camera orbit.Pitch = 0.5 orbit.Ground = world.GroundHeight // it never goes under the ground view := models.Camera{Far: 20000} app.Run(func(frame app.Frame) bool { // The circle pad, from −1 to 1 each way: turn left and right, tilt up and down. circleX, circleY := frame.Reading.Circle() orbit.Yaw -= circleX * 1.8 * frame.Seconds orbit.Pitch += circleY * 1.2 * frame.Seconds // The cross is the arrows and L, R are minus and plus, which the orbit already reads; the // touch screen is left out, so a finger does not turn the island. keys := *frame.Input keys.SetButton(input.MouseLeft, false) orbit.Update(&keys, frame.Seconds, &view) renderer.Draw(world, view) // begins the frame, draws and shows it return true }) } Checkpoint The same island, and now the circle pad turns round it and tilts it, the cross does too, L and R go further and nearer. The camera never sinks under the ground. Level 3: the island, ready to be turned Bonus (optional): a slower, gentler turn Achievement unlocked: Navigator Level 4 · The Touch designer Mission Pieces Time A Go UI panel on the touch screen: the time of day bottom.New , Paint , both screens in one frame 10 min The idea The bottom screen is a touch screen , so it is the pointer: a finger or the stylus presses Go UI's buttons and drags its sliders exactly as a mouse would. bottom lays a Go UI interface out there in a theme made for fingers, in the sea's colours. Both screens are drawn in one frame : between ctr.BeginFrame and ctr.EndFrame , the island with PaintStereo (Draw would begin and end a frame of its own) and then the panel. Build it //go:build nintendo3ds // The island above, and below a go-ui panel touched with a finger: the time of day. package main import ( "fmt" "math" "github.com/akrck02/go-3ds/app" "github.com/akrck02/go-3ds/bottom" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/camera" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/ctr" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/graphics" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/input" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/models" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene/sample" ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" ) func main() { screen, err := ctr.Open() if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } defer screen.Close() renderer, err := ctr.NewSceneRenderer(screen) if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } panel, err := bottom.New(bottom.Theme()) // go-ui on the bottom screen, in a theme for fingers if err != nil { println(err.Error()) return } world := sample.Island() orbit := camera.NewOrbit(graphics.Vec4{0, 0, 0, 1}, 450) orbit.Pitch = 0.5 orbit.Ground = world.GroundHeight view := models.Camera{Far: 20000} hour, litHour := float32(10), float32(-1) app.Run(func(frame app.Frame) bool { circleX, circleY := frame.Reading.Circle() orbit.Yaw -= circleX * 1.8 * frame.Seconds orbit.Pitch += circleY * 1.2 * frame.Seconds keys := *frame.Input keys.SetButton(input.MouseLeft, false) orbit.Update(&keys, frame.Seconds, &view) // Both screens in one frame: Paint* draws inside it, where Draw would begin and end its own. ctr.BeginFrame() renderer.PaintStereo(world, view, 0, 0) // one picture: no separation between the eyes panel.Paint(frame.Input, func(context *ui.Context) { context.Box(ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(16), Gap: 12}, func() { context.Heading("The island") context.Label(fmt.Sprintf("%02d:00", int(hour))) context.SliderStep("hour", &hour, 0, 23, 1) if context.Button("Noon") { hour = 12 } }) }) ctr.EndFrame() // A new light works the island's colours out again on the processor: only once the finger // leaves the screen, or every step of a drag would stutter. if hour != litHour && !frame.Input.Button(input.MouseLeft) { light(world, hour) litHour = hour } return true }) } // light puts the sun where it is at an hour: rising in the east at six, highest at noon, setting // in the west at six in the evening. func light(world *scene.Scene, hour float32) { angle := float64(hour-6) / 12 * math.Pi elevation := math.Sin(angle) * 1.1 sun := graphics.Vec4{float32(-math.Cos(angle) * math.Cos(elevation)), float32(math.Sin(elevation)), float32(-0.35 * math.Cos(elevation)), 0} world.Environment.SunDirection = sun.Normalize() } The light is worked out again only once the finger leaves the screen: on the 3DS the island's colours are computed on the processor for each light, which would make a drag stutter. Checkpoint Below, The island , the hour and a slider: drag it and let go, and the island turns to evening or morning; Noon brings back the midday sun. Level 4: the island above, a panel with the hour and a slider below Bonus (optional): fog Achievement unlocked: Touch designer Learn more: Go UI on the 3DS Level 5 · The Stereoscopist Mission Pieces Time Real 3D with the slider ctr.Slider3D , PaintStereo with a separation 4 min The idea Your eyes are about six centimetres apart , and each sees the world a little differently; the brain makes depth of the difference. The 3DS's top screen shows each eye its own picture. The renderer draws the scene twice, from two eyes a little apart, as far apart as the 3D slider on the console's side says. Build it Only the frame changes from level 4: // The 3D slider, from 0 to 1, sets how far apart the two eyes stand: a share of the // distance to what the camera looks at. At 0 the screen shows one picture. separation := ctr.Slider3D() * float32(orbit.Distance) * 0.03 ctr.BeginFrame() renderer.PaintStereo(world, view, separation, float32(orbit.Distance)) What lies at the focal distance (the point the camera turns round) sits on the screen; nearer things come out of it, further ones go in. Checkpoint With the slider down, the same picture as before. Push it up on a console: the island stands out of the screen. (An emulator shows one eye.) Level 5: the island and the panel, ready for 3D Achievement unlocked: Stereoscopist Final challenge · Console owner Run your program on a real New 3DS: copy it to the SD card, open it from the Homebrew Launcher, and share it with the notices it must carry. Hint: the Homebrew Launcher lists the .3dsx files in /3ds/ on the SD card. A .3dsx carries TinyGo, libctru, citro3d and newlib: their licences go with it. Rare achievement unlocked: Console owner Well done All six achievements: Homebrewer, Islander, Navigator, Touch designer, Stereoscopist and Console owner You built Go for a handheld console: two screens, a 3D scene, its controls, an interface under your finger, and real 3D. Ideas to keep going Idea Difficulty Hint Fly to places on the island ⭐ cmd/explorer eases the camera to a point chosen on its panel A map of the island on the panel ⭐⭐ cmd/explorer 's islandMap : a draw2d.Image drawn from world.GroundHeight A Go UI application, unchanged ⭐⭐ Go UI's window.Run on its feature/3ds branch puts the scene above and the interface below Sound ⭐⭐ Go Sound plays through the DSP; it needs /3ds/dspfirm.cdc Troubleshooting You see Why, and what to do An exception occurred … Undefined Instruction , PC 0 Something of ctr was used before ctr.Open , such as OpenBottomConsole : open first Exception Type: Break when drawing both screens Draw begins and ends its own frame: inside BeginFrame … EndFrame , use PaintStereo build constraints exclude all Go files with go build These programs are for TinyGo's nintendo3ds target only Works in the emulator, stops on the console The emulator forgives reads of unmapped memory: run it with Go for 3DS's tools/run-in-azahar.sh , which warns of them A drag on the panel stutters Work done every frame on the processor: do it when the finger leaves ( !frame.Input.Button(input.MouseLeft) ) ← All the documentation

what-is-where.title: What is where
what-is-where.text: What is where The packages of Go for 3DS, the explorer it comes with, what you need to build for the console, and what was checked on a real New 3DS XL. What is where Piece What it does bottom A Go UI interface on the bottom screen: Go UI lays it out, Go Renderer's ctr.FlatRenderer paints it, the touch screen is its pointer. bottom.Theme is Go UI's dark theme made for 320 × 240 pixels a finger touches, in the sea's colours. app The program loop: the New 3DS's fast clock, the controls into the input state every frame (Go Renderer's ctr.Controls : the cross as arrows, L and R as minus and plus, A Enter, B Escape and back, the touch screen as the pointer), START or the HOME menu to stop. cmd/explorer The sample island on the top screen, in 3D with the slider, and a Go UI panel on the bottom one: places to fly to, the time of day and the fog, and how fast frames go. The circle pad or the cross turn the camera, L and R move it away and closer. tools/run-in-azahar.sh Runs a .3dsx in the Azahar emulator without a screen (under Xvfb) and prints what the program wrote to the debug log; it also warns about reads and writes of unmapped memory, which stop a program on the console but not in the emulator. The explorer The map is a picture the explorer draws when it starts, from the island's heights ( world.GroundHeight ): coloured by height like a chart, shaded as if lit from the north-west, with a dot on the village and one on the peak. Flying to a place eases the camera there in under a second. The time of day changes the light when the finger leaves the screen: a new light works the meshes' colours out again on the processor, which would make every step of a drag stutter. Both screens are drawn in one frame: the island with ctr.SceneRenderer.PaintStereo , the panel with bottom.Interface.Paint , between ctr.BeginFrame and ctr.EndFrame . A Go UI program with window.Run can also run on the console unchanged: Go UI's own window for the 3DS (its feature/3ds branch) puts the scene above and the interface below, and SELECT swaps them. The packages here are for programs with a loop of their own, like the explorer. What you need A TinyGo with the nintendo3ds target (a fork of TinyGo, feature/3ds ), built against a system LLVM. devkitPro's 3DS packages (devkitARM, libctru, citro3d, 3dstools) in /opt/devkitpro . tinygo build -target=nintendo3ds -o explorer.3dsx ./cmd/explorer Copy the .3dsx to /3ds/ on the SD card and open it from the Homebrew Launcher. What was checked On a New 3DS XL: the explorer at 60 frames a second, steady while the camera moves fast (GPU about 6 ms a frame, processor under 1 ms), in 3D with the slider. Its Go UI panel is checked in the Azahar emulator: tabs, buttons, the slider and the switch answer clicks on the bottom screen. Before writing a larger program The explorer is small. A program with a large scene and an interface of its own (a few hundred things on screen, data read at start) ran into the console's limits first, and these were the ways through. Each repository keeps the part that is its own: Where What it says tinygo-3ds, NINTENDO3DS.md How the heap is used, what makes garbage in TinyGo that would not in Go, how to find where it comes from, and the New 3DS's fast mode Go Renderer, docs/3ds.md Keeping a frame short: what the overlay costs, pixel-art shapes, the scene's drawing in both eyes, waiting for the GPU Go UI, docs/3ds.md Writing an interface for the console: frame times, themes, closures, texts, game looks, the buttons In short: measure on the console by phase, make no garbage in a steady frame, and keep what changes every frame small. Not yet The second core and the New 3DS's C-stick. Sound, files on the SD card (TinyGo's os has no file system there yet), the keyboard applet.
